canonical_statement: The Heart-2 phase 1 study evaluated the safety and pharmacodynamic effects of a single VERVE-102 infusion in adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or premature coronary artery disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The objectives were to assess safety and changes in blood PCSK9 protein and LDL cholesterol levels.

canonical_statement: Heart-2 was an open-label, single-ascending-dose phase 1 study.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In this phase 1, open-label, single-ascending-dose study

canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults 18 to 70 years old with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or premature coronary artery disease.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Adults 18 to 70 years of age were eligible for inclusion if they had a diagnosis of heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or premature coronary artery disease

population.label: Eligible adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or premature coronary artery disease
inclusion_criteria: Diagnosis of heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or premature coronary artery disease

canonical_statement: Premature coronary artery disease was defined as disease occurring at 55 years of age or younger in men or 65 years of age or younger in women.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: premature coronary artery disease (defined as disease occurrence at ≤55 years of age in men or at ≤65 years of age in women)

population.label: Participants meeting the premature coronary artery disease definition
inclusion_criteria: Premature coronary artery disease at ≤55 years in men or ≤65 years in women

canonical_statement: Participants were required to have fasting LDL cholesterol of at least 70 mg/dL while receiving the maximum tolerated dose of oral lipid-lowering therapy with a statin with or without ezetimibe.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants had to have a fasting LDL cholesterol level of at least 70 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter) while receiving the maximum tolerated dose of oral lipid-lowering therapy (a statin with or without ezetimibe).

population.label: Eligible participants
inclusion_criteria: Fasting LDL cholesterol ≥70 mg/dL while receiving maximum tolerated oral lipid-lowering therapy (statin with or without ezetimibe)

canonical_statement: Reported exclusion criteria included uncontrolled hypertension, inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, and ongoing PCSK9 inhibitor treatment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Exclusion criteria included uncontrolled hypertension, inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus, and ongoing use of a PCSK9 inhibitor treatment.

canonical_statement: VERVE-102 consists of mRNA encoding adenine base-editor protein version 8.8 and a guide RNA targeting PCSK9, encapsulated in a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: VERVE-102 consists of an mRNA encoding an adenine base-editor protein (version 8.8) and a guide RNA targeting PCSK9, which are encapsulated by a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle.

exposures.details: mRNA encoding adenine base-editor protein version 8.8 plus guide RNA targeting PCSK9 in a GalNAc-lipid nanoparticle

canonical_statement: VERVE-102 targets a splice site at the 5′ end of intron 1 of PCSK9; the intended A·T-to-G·C base edit enables read-through to a stop codon that prevents hepatic PCSK9 expression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Altering the splice site enables read-through to a stop codon that prevents translation and expression of PCSK9 protein.

canonical_statement: In vitro off-target screening in primary human hepatocytes was reported as showing VERVE-102 editing specific to the target site in PCSK9.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Editing with VERVE-102 was specific for the target site in PCSK9 in off-target screening experiments involving primary human hepatocytes in vitro

canonical_statement: In nonhuman primates, reported biodistribution across 26 tissues showed high PCSK9 editing activity in liver and low editing in adrenal glands and spleen.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the biodistribution of PCSK9 editing across 26 tissues supported high levels of editing activity in the liver and low levels of editing in the adrenal glands and spleen

canonical_statement: Offspring of mice given an orthologous Pcsk9-targeting mouse equivalent of VERVE-102 showed no transmission of the Pcsk9 edit, which the authors described as consistent with absence of parental germline editing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Assessment of the offspring of mice that had been given an orthologous mouse equivalent of VERVE-102, with a guide RNA targeting mouse Pcsk9, showed no transmission of the Pcsk9 edit, which is consistent with an absence of editing of the parental germline

canonical_statement: Participants received one intravenous infusion of VERVE-102 at 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, or 1.0 mg total RNA/kg over up to approximately 4 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants received a single intravenous infusion of VERVE-102 at one of six weight-based doses (0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, or 1.0 mg of total RNA per kilogram of body weight) over a period of up to approximately 4 hours.

canonical_statement: All participants received dexamethasone before infusion and dexamethasone plus histamine H1- and H2-receptor antagonists on the infusion day to reduce infusion-reaction risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Premedication was administered to all the participants to reduce the risk of infusion-related reactions and consisted of dexamethasone on the day before VERVE-102 infusion and dexamethasone plus a histamine H1–receptor antagonist and histamine H2–receptor antagonist on the day of infusion.

canonical_statement: Participants were observed as inpatients for at least 2 days, assessed daily through day 4, weekly through day 28, and then at days 60, 90, 180, 270, and 365.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Participants underwent inpatient observation for at least 2 days and daily clinical and laboratory assessments through day 4. Subsequent follow-up was weekly through day 28, with additional scheduled visits on days 60, 90, 180, 270, and 365.

canonical_statement: Dose escalation occurred after review by an independent data and safety monitoring board.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Data were reviewed by the independent data and safety monitoring board before dose escalation.

canonical_statement: The primary objective was safety; adverse events were graded using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary objective was to assess the safety of VERVE-102... Adverse events were graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, version 5.0.

outcome.definition: Safety events graded according to CTCAE version 5.0

canonical_statement: Secondary pharmacodynamic objectives included percent and absolute change from baseline in plasma PCSK9 and fasting LDL cholesterol levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Secondary objectives were to characterize the pharmacokinetics of VERVE-102 and to evaluate pharmacodynamic effects, which were measured as the percent change and the absolute change from baseline in plasma PCSK9 and fasting LDL cholesterol levels.

concept.text: Plasma PCSK9 and fasting LDL cholesterol change from baseline

outcome.definition: Percent and absolute change from baseline

canonical_statement: Where indicated, pharmacodynamic effects were summarized as time-averaged values from day 28 through each participant’s last follow-up using trapezoidal-rule area-under-the-curve analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: pharmacodynamic data, where indicated, are reported as the time-averaged values of the variable from day 28 through the participant’s last follow-up visit on the basis of an area-under-the-curve analysis performed with the trapezoidal rule.

canonical_statement: The trial was designed to enroll up to 85 participants; this interim analysis was nonprespecified and used no formal statistical testing.
